lessons.title: Lesson 1: JavaScript Basics
lessons.html:
Your First JavaScript Program

JavaScript makes websites interactive. Runs in browser and on servers (Node.js).

Hello World:

<script>
console.log("Hello, JavaScript!");
alert("Welcome!");

// Write to page
document.write("<h1>Hello!</h1>");
</script>

Where to Put JavaScript:

  • <script> in HTML
  • external.js file: <script src="script.js"></script>

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Variables & Data Types
lessons.html:
Storing Data

JavaScript variables hold data. Use let, const, var.

Basic Types:

TypeExample
Number42, 3.14
String"Hello", 'World'
Booleantrue, false
Array[1, 2, 3]
let name = "Alice";     // String
let age = 25;          // Number
const PI = 3.14;       // Constant
let scores = [90, 85]; // Array

console.log(`Hi ${name}, you are ${age}`);

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Functions
lessons.html:
Reusable Code Blocks

Functions perform tasks. Can take inputs (parameters) and return values.

Function Examples:

// Declare function
function greet(name) {
    return "Hello, " + name + "!";
}
// Arrow function (modern)
const add = (a, b) => a + b;
const multiply = (x, y) => {
    console.log(`${x} * ${y}`);
    return x * y;
};
console.log(greet("Bob"));  // Hello, Bob!
console.log(add(5, 3));      // 8

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Conditions & Loops
lessons.html:
Control Flow

Make decisions and repeat code.

if/else:

let age = 20;
if (age >= 18) {
    console.log("Adult");
} else {
    console.log("Minor");
}

Loops:

// for loop
for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
    console.log(i);  // 0 1 2 3 4
}
// for...of (arrays)
let fruits = ["apple", "banana", "orange"];
for (let fruit of fruits) {
    console.log(fruit);
}

lessons.title: Lesson 5: DOM Manipulation
lessons.html:
Make Pages Interactive

Change HTML/CSS from JavaScript.

Select Elements:

<button id="myButton">Click me</button>
<div id="output"></div>
const button = document.getElementById("myButton");
const output = document.getElementById("output");

// Add click event
button.onclick = function() {
    output.innerHTML = "<h2>Button clicked!</h2>";
    output.style.color = "blue";
};
